arxiv-1901-00547.title: Probing the Accretion Induced Collapse of White Dwarfs in Millisecond Pulsars
arxiv-1901-00547.creator: Ali Taani, Awni Khasawneh
arxiv-1901-00547.description: Abstract This paper investigates the progenitors of Millisecond Pulsars (MSPs) with a distribution of long orbital periods (P orb > 2 \rm{}_{orb}>2 d), to show the link between white dwarf (WD) binaries and long orbits for some binary MSPs through the Accretion Induced Collapse (AIC) of a WD.

arxiv-2105-08847.title: Beyond “Fairness:” Structural (In)justice Lenses on AI for Education
arxiv-2105-08847.creator: Michael Madaio, Su Lin Blodgett, Elijah Mayfield, Ezekiel Dixon-Román
arxiv-2105-08847.description: Abstract Educational technologies, and the systems of schooling in which they are deployed, enact particular ideologies about what is important to know and how learners should learn. As artificial intelligence technologies—in education and beyond—may contribute to inequitable outcomes for marginalized communities, various approaches have been developed to evaluate and mitigate the harmful impacts of AI.

arxiv-2305-13809.title: Towards the horizons of Tits’s vision — on band schemes, crowds and 𝔽 1 {\mathbb{F}}_{1} -structures
arxiv-2305-13809.creator: Oliver Lorscheid, Koen Thas
arxiv-2305-13809.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Oliver Lorscheid, Koen Thas. This text is dedicated to Jacques Tits’s ideas on geometry over 𝔽 1 {{\mathbb{F}}_{1}} , the field with one element. In a first part, we explain how thin Tits geometries surface as rational point sets over the Krasner hyperfield, which links these ideas to combinatorial flag varieties in the sense of Borovik, Gelfand and White and 𝔽 1 {{\mathbb{F}}_{1}} -geometry in the sense of Connes and Consani.

arxiv-2310-01875.title: Towards Stable Backdoor Purification through Feature Shift Tuning
arxiv-2310-01875.creator: Rui Min, Zeyu Qin, Li Shen, Minhao Cheng
arxiv-2310-01875.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Rui Min, Zeyu Qin, Li Shen, Minhao Cheng. It has been widely observed that deep neural networks (DNN) are vulnerable to backdoor attacks where attackers could manipulate the model behavior maliciously by tampering with a small set of training samples. Although a line of defense methods is proposed to mitigate this threat, they either require complicated modifications to the training process or heavily rely on the specific model architecture, which makes them hard to deploy into real-world applications.

arxiv-2311-01553.title: Total Variation Meets Differential Privacy
arxiv-2311-01553.creator: Elena Ghazi ∗ , Ibrahim Issa ∗ †
arxiv-2311-01553.description: Abstract The framework of approximate differential privacy is considered, and augmented by leveraging the notion of “the total variation of a (privacy-preserving) mechanism” (denoted by η \eta -TV). With this refinement, an exact composition result is derived, and shown to be significantly tighter than the optimal bounds for differential privacy (which do not consider the total variation).

arxiv-2312-12288.title: New Qutrit Codes from Pure and Bordered Multidimensional Circulant Construction Note: This material is based upon work supported by the National Science Foundation under Grant DMS-2243991.
arxiv-2312-12288.creator: Padmapani Seneviratne, Hannah Cuff, Alexandra Koletsos, Kerry Seekamp, Adrian Thananopavarn
arxiv-2312-12288.description: Abstract We use multidimensional circulant approach to construct new qutrit stabilizer ⟦ ℓ , 0 , d ⟧ \llbracket\ell,0,d\rrbracket codes with parameters ( ℓ , d ) ∈ { ( 51 , 16 ) , ( 52 , 16 ) , ( 54 , 17 ) , ( 55 , 17 ) , ( 57 , 17 ) } (\ell,d)\in\{(51,16),(52,16),(54,17),(55,17),(57,17)\}

arxiv-2402-12929.title: Weight decomposition of 𝔰 ​ 𝔩 d ​ ( ℝ ) \mathfrak{sl}_{d}({\mathbb{R}}) with respect to the adjoint representation of 𝔰 ​ 𝔬 ​ ( p , q ) \mathfrak{so}(p,q)
arxiv-2402-12929.creator: Jiyoung Han
arxiv-2402-12929.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Jiyoung Han. In this concise article, we compute the weight decomposition of 𝔰 ​ 𝔩 d ​ ( ℝ ) \mathfrak{sl}_{d}({\mathbb{R}}) with respect to the adjoint representation of 𝔰 ​ 𝔬 ​ ( p , q ) \mathfrak{so}(p,q) , where d = p + q d=p+q and demonstrate in detail that 𝔰 ​ 𝔩 d ​ ( ℝ ) \mathfrak{sl}_{d}({\mathbb{R}}) comprises two irreducible 𝔰 ​ 𝔬 ​ ( p , q ) \mathfrak{so}(p,q) -invariant subspaces.

arxiv-2403-11288.title: Benefits of non-adiabatic quantum control in quantum computation through spin qubit systems
arxiv-2403-11288.creator: Nirupam Dutta
arxiv-2403-11288.description: Abstract This is evident that the controllable quantum systems can be the reliable building blocks for Quantum computation. In reality we are witnessing the progress towards making the idea tractable enough, though optimistic but the threshold is not very near to us. The dawn of quantum computation has begun.

arxiv-2408-09985.title: Ocean Circulation on Tide-locked Lava Worlds, Part II: Scalings
arxiv-2408-09985.creator: Yanhong Lai, Wanying Kang, Jun Yang
arxiv-2408-09985.description: Abstract On tidally locked lava planets, magma ocean can form on the permanent dayside. The circulation of the magma ocean can be driven by stellar radiation and atmospheric winds. The strength of ocean circulation and the depth of the magma ocean depend on external forcings and the dominant balance of the momentum equation.

arxiv-2410-00480.title: Stability analysis of chaotic systems in latent spaces
arxiv-2410-00480.creator: Elise Özalp, Luca Magri
arxiv-2410-00480.description: Abstract Partial differential equations, and their chaotic solutions, are pervasive in the modelling of complex systems in engineering, science, and beyond. Data-driven methods can find solutions to partial differential equations with a divide-and-conquer strategy: The solution is sought in a latent space, on which the temporal dynamics are inferred (“latent-space” approach).

arxiv-2502-02688.title: Efficient Implementation of the Global Cardinality Constraint with Costs
arxiv-2502-02688.creator: Margaux SCHMIED, Jean-Charles REGIN
arxiv-2502-02688.description: Abstract The success of Constraint Programming relies partly on the global constraints and implementation of the associated filtering algorithms. Recently, new ideas emerged to improve these implementations in practice, especially regarding the all different constraint. In this paper, we consider the cardinality constraint with costs.

arxiv-2509-04779.title: Decoders Laugh as Loud as Encoders
arxiv-2509-04779.creator: Eli Borodach, Raj Dandekar, Rajat Dandekar, Sreedath Panat
arxiv-2509-04779.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Eli Borodach, Raj Dandekar, Rajat Dandekar, Sreedath Panat. From the dawn of the computer, Allen Turing dreamed of a robot that could communicate using language as a human being. The recent advances in the field of Large Language Models (LLMs) shocked the scientific community when a single model can apply for various natural language processing (NLP) tasks, while the output results are sometimes even better than most human communication skills. Models such as GPT, Claude, Grok, etc.

arxiv-2601-11279.title: Measurements of electroweak penguin and lepton-flavor violating B B decays to final states with missing energy at Belle and Belle II
arxiv-2601-11279.creator: Gaetano de Marino, on behalf of the Belle II collaboration
arxiv-2601-11279.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Gaetano de Marino, on behalf of the Belle II collaboration. The Belle and Belle II experiments have collected a 1.2 ab − 1 $1.2\text{\,}\mathrm{a}\mathrm{b}$^{-1} sample of collisions at a center-of-mass energy corresponding to the Υ ⁡ ( 4 ​ S ) \Upsilon(4S) resonance. These datasets, with low particle multiplicity and constrained initial state kinematics, are an ideal environment to search for rare electroweak penguin B B decays and lepton-flavor-violating B B decays to final states with missing energy from neutrinos.

plos-pone-0001754.title: The Impact of the Human DNA Topoisomerase II C-Terminal Domain on Activity
plos-pone-0001754.creator: Emma L. Meczes, Kathryn L. Gilroy, Katherine L. West et al.
plos-pone-0001754.description: PLOS ONE research article. Type II DNA topoisomerases (topos) are essential enzymes needed for the resolution of topological problems that occur during DNA metabolic processes. Topos carry out an ATP-dependent strand passage reaction whereby one double helix is passed through a transient break in another.

pmc-10537789.title: The Antiviral Factor SERINC5 Impairs the Expression of Non-Self-DNA
pmc-10537789.creator: Yuhang Shi, Sydney Simpson, Shahad K Ahmed, Yuexuan Chen, Aidin Tavakoli-Tameh, Sanath Kumar Janaka, David T Evans, Ruth Serra-Moreno, Luis Menéndez-Arias
pmc-10537789.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). SERINC5 is a restriction factor that becomes incorporated into nascent retroviral particles, impairing their ability to infect target cells. In turn, retroviruses have evolved countermeasures against SERINC5. For instance, the primate lentiviruses (HIV and SIV) use Nef, Moloney Murine Leukemia Virus (MLV) uses GlycoGag, and Equine Infectious Anemia Virus (EIAV) uses S2 to remove SERINC5 from the plasma membrane, preventing its incorporation into progeny virions.

pmc-10737750.title: HUMAN FACTORS ISSUES IN THE DESIGN OF VIRTUAL REALITY TO SUPPORT OLDER ADULTS’ SOCIAL AND COGNITIVE ENGAGEMENT
pmc-10737750.creator: Veronica Falcon Borbolla, Walter Boot, Andrew Dilanchian, Ana Sophia Garces Torres, Mario Hernandez, Bill Tong Xu, Armin Mostafavi, Benjamin Kim
pmc-10737750.description: Emerging technologies such as virtual reality (VR) hold tremendous potential to improve the lives of older adults, including the opportunity to support social and cognitive engagement. However, this potential will only be realized if VR technologies and applications (apps) are well-designed, considering the needs, preferences, and abilities of older people.

pmc-11360467.title: Spatial Augmented Reality for Expanding the Reach of Individuals with Tremor beyond Their Physical Limits
pmc-11360467.creator: Kai Wang, Mengjing Wu, Zhi Sun, Qun Huang, Raffaele Bruno
pmc-11360467.description: Tremor is a prevalent neurological disorder characterized by involuntary shaking or trembling of body parts. This condition impairs fine motor skills and hand coordination to varying degrees and can even affect overall body mobility. As a result, tremors severely disrupt the daily lives and work of those affected, significantly limiting their physical activity space.

pmc-11438041.title: Efficacy and safety of thalidomide for recurrent aphthous stomatitis: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
pmc-11438041.creator: Yang Jian, Fuqin Wang, Minru Zhao, Xianru Han, Xiaoyu Wang
pmc-11438041.description: BackgroundRecurrent aphthous stomatitis (RAS) is considered as the most common oral mucosal lesion affecting up to 25% of people worldwide. Thalidomide has been reported for the treatment of RAS, but the evidence has not been systematically evaluated. We first systematically reviewed the efficacy and safety of thalidomide for the treatment of RAS.

pmc-11476915.title: Development History, Structure, and Function of ASR (Abscisic Acid-Stress-Ripening) Transcription Factor
pmc-11476915.creator: Yue Zhang, Mengfan Wang, Andery V. Kitashov, Ling Yang
pmc-11476915.description: Abiotic and biotic stress factors seriously affect plant growth and development. The process of plant response to abiotic stress involves the synergistic action of multiple resistance genes. The ASR (Abscisic acid stress-ripening) gene is a plant-specific transcription factor that plays a central role in regulating plant senescence, fruit ripening, and response to abiotic stress.

pmc-11513117.title: Lightening the mind with audiovisual stimulation as an accessible alternative to breath-focused meditation for mood and cognitive enhancement
pmc-11513117.creator: Micah Alan Johnson, Ninette Simonian, Nicco Reggente
pmc-11513117.description: In this randomized, controlled, and double-blind experiment with a relatively large sample (n = 262), a novel technique of audiovisual stimulation (AVS) was demonstrated to substantially improve self-reported mood states by reducing several negative affects, including anxiety and depression, and enhancing performance on mood-sensitive cognitive tasks.

pmc-11633950.title: The first-person effect. A reconsideration of two meta-analyses
pmc-11633950.creator: Klaus Moser, Karsten I. Paul, Roman Soucek, Anett Eskofier, Nathalie Galais
pmc-11633950.description: The third-person effect describes a tendency to estimate the influence of mass communication on others (“third persons”) as being stronger than on oneself and this has been well documented in previous research. Though a first-person effect has also been postulated for desirable mass communication messages (for ex.

pmc-11647140.title: Vaccination coverage and access among children and adult migrants and refugees in the Middle East and North African region: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-11647140.creator: Oumnia Bouaddi, Farah Seedat, Hassan Edries Hasaan Mohammed, Stella Evangelidou, Anna Deal, Ana Requena-Méndez, Mohamed Khalis, Sally Hargreaves, Middle East and North Africa Migrant Health Working Group
pmc-11647140.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). SummaryBackgroundThe Middle East and North African (MENA) region is a major global hotspot for migration with more than 40 million migrants, who may be an under-vaccinated group because of barriers to vaccination within countries of origin, transit, and destination.

pmc-12466830.title: Breaking the Cycle: How Coping and Flexibility Disrupt the Link Between Kinesiophobia and Rumination in Athletes
pmc-12466830.creator: Osman Pepe, Mehmet Behzat Turan, İbrahim Dalbudak, Berat Koçyiğit, Gül Bahar Bayıroğlu, Melih Balyan, Olcay Mülazımoğlu, Sevim Kır
pmc-12466830.description: Background: This study aims to examine the relationship between Kinesiophobia and Rumination in athletes, and to reveal the mediating roles of Coping Responses and Psychological Flexibility in this relationship. Methods: Three hundred ninety licensed athletes, including 225 females and 165 males, voluntarily participated in the study. Participants were selected through simple random sampling from various sports clubs across Turkey.

pmc-12473924.title: Intelligent Soft Sensor for Spindle Convective Heat Transfer Coefficient Under Varying Operating Conditions Using Improved Grey Wolf Optimization Algorithm
pmc-12473924.creator: Jinxiang Pian, Gen Li
pmc-12473924.description: The thermal deformation of high-precision CNC machine tools has long been a significant barrier to improving machining accuracy. Accurately characterizing the thermal properties of the spindle, especially the convective heat transfer coefficients (CHTC), is essential for precise thermal analysis. However, due to the lack of dedicated instruments for directly measuring the CHTC, thermal analysis of the spindle faces substantial challenges.

pmc-12573804.title: Rational Design of Zwitterionic Polymers with Tunable Phase Separation Propensity
pmc-12573804.creator: Timo N. Schneider, Suiying Ye, Nicola Carrara, Umberto Capasso Palmiero, Matteo Salvalaglio, Paolo Arosio
pmc-12573804.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Zwitterionic polymers are emerging as promising candidates for forming fluid-like coacervates with desirable characteristics, including antifouling capabilities, stimulus responsiveness, and biocompatibility. These attributes make them particularly appealing for applications in the biomedical field, including bioseparation, biochemical analysis, and diagnostics. However, there are currently no clear guiding principles for predicting the phase separation behavior of zwitterionic polymers and informing the design of novel phase-separating polymers.

pmc-12610653.title: Myosin-19 and Miro Regulate Mitochondria–Endoplasmic Reticulum Contacts and Mitochondria Inner Membrane Architecture
pmc-12610653.creator: Aya Attia, Katarzyna Majstrowicz, Samruddhi Shembekar, Ulrike Honnert, Petra Nikolaus, Birgit Lohmann, Martin Bähler, Francisco Rivero, Miguel Vicente Manzanares
pmc-12610653.description: Mitochondrial dynamics are important for cellular health and include morphology, fusion, fission, vesicle formation, transport and contact formation with other organelles. Myosin XIX (Myo19) is an actin-based motor, which competes with TRAK1/2 adaptors of microtubule-based motors for binding to the outer mitochondrial membrane receptors Mitochondrial Rho GTPases 1/2 (Miro). Currently, it is poorly understood how Myo19 contributes to mitochondrial dynamics.

pmc-12860036.title: Role of Trichostatin A (TSA) in modulating the epigenetic modification in the lymphocytes of colorectal cancer (CRC)
pmc-12860036.creator: R. Ilaya Kumar, Kavya Jain, Harshnna Gururajan, Karan Raj Rai, Melvin George, Koustav Sarkar
pmc-12860036.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Trichostatin A (TSA) is a strong epigenetic tool that promises to have the future in the field of immune reprogramming, but its mechanisms of action in patient-derived immune cells in colorectal cancer (CRC) are still poorly studied. We examined in this current study the molecular and functional immune phenotype of lymphocytes of CRC patients and healthy donors in response to low-dose (0.1 nM), short-term (12 h) treatment with TSA, which aims at narrowing cytotoxicity and retaining epigenetic regulation.

pmc-13479624.title: Assessment of macrolide resistance in the respiratory tract of preterm-born infants during treatment with azithromycin in the AZTEC clinical trial
pmc-13479624.creator: Ali F Aboklaish, W John Watkins, David Gallacher, Claudia Consoli, John Lowe, Julian R Marchesi, Sailesh Kotecha
pmc-13479624.description: BackgroundOur multicentre, double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled Azithromycin therapy for prevention of chronic lung disease of prematurity trial assessed if early 10-day azithromycin treatment improved survival without development of chronic lung disease of prematurity when compared with placebo in 796 preterm-born infants. Since antibiotic resistance remains a significant global health priority, we had preplanned macrolide-resistance assessment in recruited infants.

pmc-13587248.title: Medicaid waiver-based housing supports in a safety-net setting: utilization and spending outcomes
pmc-13587248.creator: Nicole C McCann, Heather E Hsu, Stephanie Ettinger de Cuba, Jasper Frank, Paulina Lange, Michael D Stein, Paul R Shafer
pmc-13587248.description: IntroductionStates have expanded Medicaid waiver-based housing support programs, but evidence on outcomes in safety-net settings is limited.MethodsWe evaluated health care utilization and spending associated with Massachusetts Medicaid's Flexible Services Program housing supports (FSP-H), provided to Accountable Care Organization (ACO) members with housing-related needs and qualifying health risks (2021-2024).

pmc-13623805.title: Reconstructing mental representations of block towers: A new bias for physical stability in visual working memory
pmc-13623805.creator: Stefan Uddenberg, Jun Kwak, Brian J Scholl

pmc-13652445.title: Myxoma of the round ligament mimicking femoral hernia: a diagnostic surprise in the operating room
pmc-13652445.creator: Imen Ben Ismail, Rime Amari, Mouna Mlika, Marwen Sghaier, Hakim Zenaidi, Saber Rebii
pmc-13652445.description: Introduction:Groin swellings in adult women are most commonly attributed to inguinal or femoral hernias. However, rare neoplasms arising from the round ligament of the uterus may present with similar clinical features, posing significant diagnostic challenges. Myxomas are benign mesenchymal tumors characterized by an abundant myxoid stroma, but their occurrence in the round ligament is exceedingly rare.
